label: Skeleton
title: Skeleton
summary: Use a Skeleton group to show the shape of content while it loads, so the screen doesn't jump when it arrives.
corePrinciple: Show the shape of what's coming, then fill it in place.

anatomy.title: Grey blocks with a moving highlight
anatomy.description: Each placeholder is a light grey block whose kind sets its corners. While the group loads, a white band sweeps across every block, one after another.

configuration.title: Four kinds, or components that draw their own
configuration.description: A Skeleton's kind sets only its corners; its width and height are yours. Inside a group, Coin components such as Text, Avatar, Badge, and Button draw their own placeholder at their own size, so you rarely place a Skeleton by hand.

The default kind: square sizes make a circle, wide ones a pill, for avatars and buttons.

states.title: Loading, loaded, and reduced motion
states.description: The group's loading flag switches every placeholder inside it at once. While loading, a white band sweeps across the blocks every 1.5 s, each a little after the one before. When the device asks for reduced motion, or the group sets it, the blocks pulse gently instead.
blocks: Placeholders hold the layout, and the shimmer runs down them in a cascade.
The same components show their content in the same places.
A slow white pulse every 3 s replaces the moving band.
loading on its own draws that line’s placeholder too, and screen readers hear “Loading”.

sizing.title: The size of what it replaces
sizing.description: Coin components size their own placeholders: a Text bar is as tall as its line and about as long as its words, and an Avatar's is its own size. A hand-placed Skeleton has no size until you give it a width and height; percentages follow its host.

content.title: Mirror the real layout
content.description: Put the same components in the group that will show the content, with realistic sample text, so each placeholder has the right length. Anything already known, such as a heading, stays real with loading off.
blocks: The title stays readable; only the values still loading turn into placeholders.

sources.title: Use the public Skeleton contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Coin variables with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: No Skeleton component; only its colour and corner variables

Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma has no Skeleton component: the Coin variables hold its grey and its corner radii, and the ticket’s Figma link opens the Stepper Item page. In code a SkeletonGroup switches every placeholder inside it; Text, Avatar, Badge, Button, Image, and other Coin components draw their own, and a Skeleton places one by hand. Blocks are light grey (#e7e7e7; the old Storybook page gives a lighter grey). A white band sweeps across them every 1.5 s in a 75 ms cascade, or they pulse every 3 s with reduced motion, as in Storybook. Since the #266 fix a component’s loading draws its placeholder without a group too, named “Loading”; inside a group the blocks are hidden from screen readers and the group announces “Loading” once. A Skeleton placed by hand still needs a group. The published Storybook page is still the old generated one.
